title: The One Thing
coreMove: Name the single concern or task that carries the most leverage before spending energy anywhere else.
sourcePressure: Chapter 1 introduces the governing idea through the City Slickers frame, overextension, uneven focus, and the claim that the most important task makes other work easier or unnecessary.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Telling the reader to choose one favorite task and ignore the rest.

hook: A single choice changes the whole day
The real priority is hiding under the busy work
The One Thing as a generic focus opener
counterintuition: Focus is harder than it looks
tryThisNow: Set a timer and list priorities
Write down your one thing without a concrete context
examples: generic office worker choosing email or strategy

exampleSpecs.domain: emergency room triage board during a storm surge
exampleSpecs.stakes: six waiting patients and one trauma bay left
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the nurse wipes three names off the side board, circles the one patient whose airway decision unlocks the room, and sends the team there first
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a rain-dark ER board with colored magnets sliding under a nurse's thumb

exampleSpecs.domain: artisan bakery facing a failed wholesale order before dawn
exampleSpecs.stakes: a hotel delivery leaves in forty minutes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the baker stops fixing all trays, weighs the rye batch that can save the invoice, and tells the team to leave the pastry defects alone
exampleSpecs.firstImage: flour on a loading-dock scale beside one crate of dark loaves

exampleSpecs.domain: public defender preparing for a bail docket
exampleSpecs.stakes: one client may sleep in jail because of a missing record
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the attorney closes five minor case folders and pulls the one file where a phone call to probation changes the hearing
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a courthouse hallway bench with six manila folders and one red sticky note

exampleSpecs.domain: theater stage manager before opening night
exampleSpecs.stakes: a sold-out preview depends on one unsafe fly cue
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she stops polishing every cue sheet, marks the failing fly cue in tape, and holds the crew on that single move until it runs clean
exampleSpecs.firstImage: black gaffer tape crossing one cue line under a clip light

exampleSpecs.domain: community garden after a vandalized irrigation line
exampleSpecs.stakes: two hundred seedlings will dry out by evening
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coordinator sees that every helpful errand mattered less than locating the cracked valve that starved the beds
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a split irrigation valve hissing beside rows of drooping seedlings

exampleSpecs.domain: data center outage at a regional bank
exampleSpecs.stakes: payment processing is down while alerts flood the screen
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the lead predicts which alert controls the cascade, mutes the rest, and watches the payment queue start moving after that one service restarts
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a dark operations room with one alert pinned above a frozen payment queue

skillTargets: separate the leverage task from merely visible work
choose the concern that changes the rest of the day
notice when scattered effort is protecting comfort

tryThisNowSpec: Look at the next four hours and write the one result that would make two other tasks easier to handle or unnecessary.
